root_cause.text: In the amdxdna AIE2 context creation error path, aie2_create_context() called aie2_destroy_context() on a partially initialized amdxdna_hwctx even when hwctx->priv->mbox_chann had never been created, but aie2_destroy_context() unconditionally dereferenced that mailbox channel pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states mailbox channel creation can fail leaving the pointer NULL, while the patch changes the aie2_create_context() failure labels from calling aie2_destroy_context(ndev, hwctx) to aie2_destroy_context_req(ndev, hwctx->fw_ctx_id), and aie2_destroy_context() still directly calls xdna_mailbox_stop_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann) and xdna_mailbox_destroy_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann) without a NULL check.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to send a firmware destroy-context request and warn on failure so hardware contexts can be properly torn down.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function named aie2_destroy_context_req() was added. It takes an amdxdna_dev_hdl pointer and a u32 context ID, declares a destroy-context management message with DECLARE_AIE2_MSG(destroy_ctx, MSG_OP_DESTROY_CONTEXT), assigns req.context_id = id, sends the message via aie2_send_mgmt_msg_wait(), logs a warning with XDNA_WARN() if the send fails, and returns the resulting status code.
intent_record.how: This adds runtime support for issuing a firmware management request to destroy a context by ID and reporting failures through a warning log. It enables the driver to explicitly request context teardown from firmware, rather than lacking a dedicated destroy-context request path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fail context creation on invalid firmware context IDs and clean up created contexts when force-preempt configuration fails.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a WARN_ONCE check on hwctx->fw_ctx_id == -1 with an if statement using WARN_ON_ONCE that returns -EINVAL when the invalid context ID is detected, and changes the error path after aie2_runtime_cfg() failure from returning ret directly to jumping to del_ctx_req.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now treats an unexpected firmware context ID of -1 as a real error and aborts context creation instead of only emitting a warning and continuing. It also ensures that if enabling force preempt fails after context creation, execution follows the cleanup path to delete the created context rather than returning immediately and potentially leaving stale state behind.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix context cleanup by using the firmware-only destroy request on create failure and centralizing context deletion logic in a helper.
intent_record.what: The error paths in aie2_create_context() were changed to log a more specific IRQ allocation failure message, use a renamed cleanup label, and call aie2_destroy_context_req(ndev, hwctx->fw_ctx_id) instead of aie2_destroy_context(ndev, hwctx). In aie2_destroy_context(), the inline destroy-context mailbox message construction and fw_ctx_id == -1 early return were removed, the firmware destroy operation was replaced with a call to aie2_destroy_context_req(ndev, hwctx->fw_ctx_id), and debug/error strings were adjusted and simplified.
intent_record.how: On create-context failure after the firmware context has been created but before mailbox channel setup completes, the code now sends only the firmware context deletion request instead of invoking the full destroy path, avoiding teardown of a mailbox channel that was never created. The destroy path also centralizes firmware context deletion through a shared helper, while still stopping and destroying the mailbox channel during normal teardown.

grouping_result.intent: Fix context cleanup by using the firmware-only destroy request on create failure and centralizing context deletion logic in a helper.

consistency_review.core_intent: Improve GPU context creation failure handling by validating firmware context IDs and centralizing proper firmware-backed context teardown in a helper.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly modify the context creation failure path and cleanup logic, specifically avoiding full context destruction on partially initialized contexts by using firmware-only teardown/centralized deletion helpers. That matches the root cause of calling destroy on a partially initialized context with an uncreated mailbox channel.

candidates.rationale: On the create-context error path, this calls the full destroy routine even when context setup is only partial. Per the root cause, that routine assumes hwctx->priv->mbox_chann exists, so invoking it before mailbox channel creation triggers the vulnerable dereference path.

This unconditionally dereferences the mailbox channel pointer in aie2_destroy_context(). If create failed before hwctx->priv->mbox_chann was initialized, this statement operates on an uncreated/NULL channel and directly embodies the crash condition.

This is another unconditional use of hwctx->priv->mbox_chann in the destroy path without checking whether the channel was ever created. It is part of the same faulty assumption that the mailbox channel always exists.

vuln_statements.explanation: This create-context error-path call invokes the full destroy routine on a partially initialized hwctx. Per the root cause, that destroy routine unconditionally dereferences hwctx->priv->mbox_chann even when it was never created, making this the statement that introduces the vulnerable path.

Inside aie2_destroy_context(), this statement unconditionally dereferences the mailbox channel pointer. When aie2_destroy_context() is reached from the partial-create failure path before mbox_chann initialization, this statement triggers the NULL/uninitialized pointer dereference.

    accel/amdxdna: Add hardware context
    
    The hardware can be shared among multiple user applications. The

    DRM_IOCTL_AMDXDNA_CREATE_HWCTX
    Allocate tile columns and create a hardware context structure to track the

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows both the creator error path and the destroy function. In `aie2_create_context()`, after firmware context creation succeeds, failures in later mailbox setup go to `out_destroy_context:`: `if (ret == -EINVAL) { ... goto out_destroy_context; }` and `if (!hwctx->priv->mbox_chann) { ... goto out_destroy_context; }`, followed by `aie2_destroy_context(ndev, hwctx);`. At that point `hwctx->fw_ctx_id` has already been set (`hwctx->fw_ctx_id = resp.context_id;`), but `hwctx->priv->mbox_chann` may still be uninitialized/NULL because channel creation either was not reached successfully or returned NULL. In `aie2_destroy_context()`, the only guard is `if (hwctx->fw_ctx_id == -1) return 0;`, then it unconditionally dereferences the mailbox channel via `xdna_mailbox_stop_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann);` and later `xdna_mailbox_destroy_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann);`. This matches the root cause exactly: destroy is called on a partially initialized context and unconditionally uses `hwctx->priv->mbox_chann`. There is no protective check like `if (hwctx->priv->mbox_chann)` before stopping/destroying the channel, so the fix is not present.
